slides.0.title: Grapes and styles
slides.0.subtitle: Tannat leads, with Muscat and Albariño behind
slides.1.title: Tannat, the national signature
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The most planted
slides.1.highlights.0.content: INAVI's 2025 register: about 1,536 ha of Tannat, 26.5% of the national total and the most planted variety
slides.1.highlights.1.title: From south-west France
slides.1.highlights.1.content: INAVI says Tannat comes from south-west France and that Uruguay is now its main producer, with more than its region of origin
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Styles
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Deep colour and firm tannin are Tannat's nature. Uruguay makes it young and easy, aged in oak, and often blended with Merlot and other varieties
slides.1.content: The one word to know for Uruguay is Tannat.
slides.2.title: The ranking by area
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Second: Muscat Hamburg
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Moscatel de Hamburgo (Muscat Hamburg) for wine covers about 17.2%, in second place. The register lists the same grape separately for table use
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Ugni Blanc and Merlot
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Each covers about a tenth of the area, close behind
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Other reds
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Cabernet Sauvignon about 5.6%, Marselan about 3.8%, Cabernet Franc about 3.5%, plus rarer French crossings such as Arinarnoa
slides.2.content: In the top four, Tannat is followed by Muscat, Ugni Blanc and Merlot.
slides.3.title: White grapes and new directions
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Albariño
slides.3.highlights.0.content: About 2.4%. INAVI says Uruguay suits it well and that it is gaining recognition, and Udelar researchers have studied it on the Atlantic east coast
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Sauvignon about 2.5% and Chardonnay about 2.0%. INAVI says the metropolitan region is especially suited to Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Viognier
slides.3.highlights.2.title: American grapes remain
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The register still includes American grapes such as Isabella (locally Frutilla) and Concord, though only in small areas
slides.3.content: Red wine leads, but whites from the Atlantic coast are building a name.
